headline: Five of seven majors overbought above their 200-day lines, while a day of BTC ETF selling sits inside a five-day net inflow
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's lopsided in a way worth naming plainly: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB are all above their 200-day trend lines, while DOGE and ADA sit below theirs. That's five above, two below, and the two laggards are also the two furthest from their 12-month highs (DOGE at -70.5%, ADA at -78.3%). This isn't a market moving as one unit. It's a majors-led advance with the smaller-cap names still digging out of a deeper hole.

Momentum is where it gets interesting. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 71.4, ETH at 70.7, SOL at 75.3, all comfortably into overbought territory, and MACD confirms the trend (above signal) on every asset except ADA. That's trend and momentum agreeing, which is straightforward, but agreement at these RSI levels also means the move has run hard and fast: BTC is up 12.9% on the week and 22.4% on the month, SOL up 23.3% on the week and 40.2% on the month. ADA is the odd one out on every axis, down 0.8% on the day even as it's up 7.8% on the week and 20.9% on the month, with MACD below signal and price below the 200-day. A stock or coin can be in an uptrend on one clock and rolling over on another; ADA is currently doing both.

Positioning tells a story of crowded longs paying for the privilege. BTC funding is running 0.0025% per 8 hours (2.7% annualized), ETH 0.0031% (3.4% annualized), both modest but positive, meaning longs are paying shorts to stay in the trade. XRP's long/short ratio of 2.47 and DOGE's 3.95 show a crowd heavily tilted to the long side on those two, and DOGE's liquidations over the last 24 hours back that up: $52,938 in longs wiped out versus just $19,806 in shorts, the opposite of BTC and ETH where shorts have taken the bigger hit ($611,471 and $630,816 respectively against much smaller long liquidations). SOL is the outlier with funding at -7.6% annualized, meaning shorts are paying longs there, an unusual setup given SOL's RSI is the highest on the board at 75.3. Crowded and expensive on the short side while price grinds higher is its own kind of fragile.

Flows add a genuine contradiction worth sitting with. On 28 Aug, BTC ETFs saw a net outflow of $201.9M, but the last five sessions net to a $924.5M inflow, and the digest flags those two windows as disagreeing. Read it as: the day was a step back inside a five-day advance, not a reversal. ETH ETFs had no such tension: inflow of $102.1M on the day, $815.7M over five sessions, and ten straight days pointing the same direction, so 'continuing' is a fair word there. Whale wallets, meanwhile, moved $176.2M net off exchanges over the last 24 hours, mostly BTC, with the biggest single moves being withdrawals from Kraken ($158.2M and $108.4M) and Coinbase Institutional ($77.8M). Zoom out to the weekly view and the last three weeks (ending Aug 15, Aug 22, Aug 29) all show net flow onto exchanges, $508M, $1,062M, and $659M respectively, an interesting tension against today's 24-hour outflow reading. Stablecoin float is up 1.11% over 30 days to $309.8B, a mild increase in dry powder rather than a surge.

Sentiment sits at 68, Greed, inside its 30-day range of 25 to 74, so the crowd is optimistic but not pinned to the top of its own recent band. That roughly matches a tape where most majors are overbought and grinding a genuine uptrend, so this isn't a case of sentiment badly lagging or leading the data; it's mostly in step, if a little warm given the whale flows moving onto exchanges over the past three weeks. What to watch from here: whether BTC funding stays positive while RSI holds above 70 (a combination that historically resolves one way or another), whether ADA reclaims its 200-day and flips MACD back above signal, and whether the next few daily ETF prints for BTC turn the five-session number negative or keep confirming the inflow trend.
